rdf:Description.dc:title: Film clip of the Rabbis' March
rdf:Description.dc:description: In 1943 a group of more than 400 rabbis, many of whom were Jewish Orthodox, demonstrated on the National Mall to urge the US to help the Jewish people of Nazi occupied Europe. Held three days before Yom Kippur, the October 6 rally generated national media attention for the Jewish leaders and their cause. Part of this attention was sparked  when President Roosevelt controversially refused to meet with the delegation. Vice President Henry Wallace met with them instead. In this video, a rabbi speaks on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial.
